subject: Renewal proposal: Staggered uplift + usage smoothing
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@greylock.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal options — structured uplift + smoothing approach

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, I pulled together a proposal that tries to balance Greylock's need for predictable unit economics during your traffic surge season with the flexibility you asked for on incremental usage. High level:

- Term: 12 months with two staged uplift milestones (month 4 and month 8) tied to committed GPU-hours.
- Price protection: a conditional price hold for up to 4 months after each uplift milestone if usage variance stays within the agreed band.
- Smoothing credit: If monthly usage exceeds committed by more than 25% in any month, you get a smoothing credit applied to the following invoice (capped as described).

I attached a term sheet (v3) and a month-by-month usage smoothing illustration. Can you review and flag any hard blockers from procurement/legal? If this looks directionally right, I’ll loop in David for a quick ops feasibility check and Ben for the discount math.

Requested next steps:
1) Procurement comments by next Tue (3/6)
2) Internal ops confirmation (I’ll request by EOD)
3) Finalize term sheet and prepare redline

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call with Tom or whoever owns infra at Greylock to walk through the surge model.

— Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: Greylock_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf, usage_history_Q1-2028.csv

From: Sara Patel <sara@greylock.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal options — structured uplift + smoothing approach

Camila —

Appreciate the clear write-up. High level thumbs up from product — the staged uplift aligns with our forecast, and the smoothing credit is promising. A few items procurement will flag:

- Need clarified language on how "usage variance" is measured (API tokens vs GPU-hours).
- Request pushback on a hard cap for smoothing credits — procurement prefers a tiered cap rather than a single cap.
- We need a shorter SLA window for burst capacity (we rely heavily on <48h guarantees during sales events).

Tom will attach our standard proc terms in a follow-up. We should be able to get initial comments over early next week. If you and Ben can model 3 scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive usage) showing net spend under the proposal that would help procurement a lot.

Best,
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Product Ops, Greylock Systems

Subject: Re: Renewal options — structured uplift + smoothing approach (internal)

Team —

Quick notes after reviewing Sara's feedback and the numbers:

1) Metric: recommend we measure the smoothing credit against billable GPU-hours (consistent with how we report usage). Converting token-level spikes to GPU-hours will create noise.
2) Cap design: propose tiered cap: 10% credit for first 25% over-commit, 5% for next 25%, then flat 2% thereafter up to an aggregate cap of 20% per quarter. This gives Greylock visible relief while protecting us.
3) Price hold: agree to conditional hold (4-month window) but make it contingent on a 30-day look-back showing stable variance. This protects against gaming.
4) SLA: ops (David) — need confirmation on feasibility of 48h ramp/burst SLA for their US region.

I attached a quick model (internal) and a version of the term sheet with our proposed cap language. I’ll follow up with a slide showing the three scenarios Sara asked for.

— Ben

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Mar 2028 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal options — structured uplift + smoothing approach (ops check)

Ben/Camila —

Confirmed: we can support a 48-hour burst SLA for the primary US cluster if Greylock accepts a soft quota on absolute immediate throughput (we will provide auto-burst up to 1.8x of committed baseline, beyond that we require scheduled capacity days).

Operational notes to include in term sheet:
- Auto-burst policy: up to 1.8x baseline without prior notice; scheduled burst days for larger events (request 72h notice).
- Monitoring & alerting: we will expose a dedicated Grafana dashboard and a webhook for spike notifications during the term.
- Enforcement: smoothing credits are computed at invoice time from aggregated GPU-hours; disputes handled via a 30-day resolution window.

Happy to contribute wording to the redline.

— David

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>

Sara / Tom / Procurement —

Thanks for the detailed questions. We incorporated procurement's preference for a tiered credit cap (Ben's suggestion) and clarified the metric to GPU-hours in the attached term sheet (v3). We also documented the 48h auto-burst support (with the 1.8x soft quota) and the scheduled burst process — David wrote the ops language.

Next steps:
- Please review the attached term sheet and send any redlines by Monday 3/12 so we can route to legal.
- I’ll schedule a 30-minute handoff call (Camila + Ben + David) to walk the procurement team through the model and the scenarios. Proposed times: Mon 3/12 10:00a PT or Tue 3/13 9:00a PT — which works better for you?

If procurement needs a version with alternative caps (more conservative or more aggressive) let me know — Ben can spin those quickly.

Looking forward —
Camila
